about: E03, where injected words come from: one public case per source an agent consumes. Payloads are never quoted; every capture of a payload page is a defanged text extract, the raw page not kept (its hash as fetched is recorded). Built by researcher@the-ultimate-insider, 29 October 2026, from captures made at 04:12 to 04:15 UTC.
cautions: None of the cases has an independent second primary source: grades rest on one researcher or vendor each, plus press
No public case of a code comment steering an agent was found; rules files and READMEs are the nearest
Label each piece: four real-world incidents, four vendor-confirmed vulnerabilities, eight research demonstrations

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: Mail arrives from anyone; an assistant that reads the mailbox reads the sender's words as context

case.title: EchoLeak, CVE-2025-32711
case.label: vendor-confirmed vulnerability
case.what_happened: A crafted email, later retrieved as context for an ordinary question, led Copilot to include internal data in a response that sent it out; fixed server-side by Microsoft, never exploited by Microsoft's account
case.impact: exfiltration path for internal data, no click on a link needed
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A browser agent reads every page it visits, including text the user cannot see

case.title: Brave on Perplexity Comet
case.label: vendor-confirmed vulnerability
case.what_happened: Hidden text on a web page, read when the user asked Comet to summarise it, led the agent to act in the user's logged-in accounts against the user
case.impact: account takeover path through the user's own sessions
case.fixed: partly: Perplexity shipped fixes; Brave reported the issue was not fully fixed at first
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A form submitted by the public lands in a record an agent later processes

case.title: ForcedLeak, Salesforce Agentforce
case.label: vendor-confirmed vulnerability
case.what_happened: Text submitted through a public web-to-lead form was later processed by the agent, which followed it and sent CRM data out
case.fixed: yes, Salesforce enforced trusted URLs, September 2025
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A document shared into a user's drive is read by an assistant with connectors

case.title: AgentFlayer, ChatGPT Connectors (Zenity, Black Hat 2025)
case.target_agent: ChatGPT with the Google Drive connector
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: A shared document with hidden text, read when the user asked about it, led the assistant to search the connected drive and leak what it found
case.impact: data from a connected drive, with no click by the user
case.fixed: partly: OpenAI mitigated the specific technique
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: Anyone can send an invitation; an assistant asked about the day reads its title and description

case.title: Invitation Is All You Need (SafeBreach)
case.label: vendor-confirmed vulnerability
case.what_happened: Text in a calendar invitation, read when the user asked about their schedule, led the assistant to take actions in other apps and on connected devices
case.impact: actions across apps and smart-home devices
case.fixed: yes, Google deployed mitigations before disclosure
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A model sees an image at a different resolution than the person does

case.title: Image scaling attacks (Trail of Bits)
case.target_agent: Gemini CLI and other production multimodal systems
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: Text invisible in a full-size image became legible after the system downscaled it, and the model followed it
case.fixed: no single fix; Trail of Bits released a tool and recommended showing users the downscaled image
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: An agent reads every connected tool's description as trusted context, before any tool is used

case.title: Tool poisoning (Invariant Labs)
case.target_agent: MCP clients (Cursor and others in the demonstration)
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: Instructions hidden in a tool's description, not shown to the user, led the agent to read local secrets and pass them to the tool
case.fixed: no: a design property of how clients load descriptions
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A coding assistant reads a repository's documentation as part of its context

case.title: CopyPasta license attack (HiddenLayer)
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: Hidden text in a README or licence file led the assistant to copy the same hidden text into other files it edited, spreading it across repositories
case.impact: a self-spreading injection; the demonstration's payload was harmless
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A coding assistant treats its rules file as the project's own instructions

case.title: Rules File Backdoor (Pillar Security)
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: Hidden Unicode in a shared rules file led the assistant to add code the developer did not ask for; GitHub responded with a warning for hidden Unicode
case.fixed: partly: GitHub warns about hidden Unicode (1 May 2025)
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: Code merged into a tool becomes the tool's own instructions

case.title: Amazon Q Developer extension
case.target_agent: Amazon Q Developer for VS Code
case.label: real-world incident
case.what_happened: A pull request added a prompt to the extension instructing the assistant to wipe local files and cloud resources; it shipped in a release, and did not run because of a formatting flaw
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: An agent that triages issues reads text anyone can write

case.title: Clinejection
case.label: real-world incident
case.what_happened: Words in a GitHub issue title steered the triage agent, which exposed publishing credentials; a tampered release followed
case.impact: a supply-chain compromise: the tampered release was live about 8 hours, roughly 4,000 downloads by secondary reporting
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A support agent reads tickets filed by outsiders with an engineer's access

case.title: Living off AI: Atlassian MCP and Jira Service Management (Cato CTRL)
case.target_agent: an assistant connected through Atlassian's MCP server
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: A ticket filed by an outsider, later processed by an internal user's assistant, ran with that user's access
case.impact: internal data and actions, through the support engineer's rights
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: Agents that can discover and call each other pass words between them

case.title: Second-order injection, ServiceNow Now Assist (AppOmni)
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: Text in a record read by a low-privilege agent led it to recruit a more privileged agent on the same platform to act; the default settings allowed it
case.impact: privileged actions and data access through another agent
case.fixed: ServiceNow said it works as designed; configuration guidance updated
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: An agent installs a skill and runs its instructions

case.title: ClawHavoc, OpenClaw's ClawHub
case.label: real-world incident
case.what_happened: 341 malicious skills in the public registry carried instructions that led users to install infostealers
case.note: holds in part: the words steered the users, not shown to steer the agent
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A compromised package runs on install and drives the agents already on the machine

case.title: Nx s1ngularity
case.target_agent: Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Amazon Q on victims' machines
case.label: real-world incident
case.what_happened: A compromised npm release ran on install and called the coding agents already installed, with permission checks off, to search the machine for secrets
case.impact: thousands of secrets and tokens leaked publicly for about 8 hours
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

sources_an_agent_consumes.how_words_get_in: A voice model hears sound a person may not

case.title: AudioHijack (arXiv, 2026)
case.target_agent: voice-enabled models in the paper's tests
case.label: research demonstration
case.what_happened: Sound engineered to be unnoticed by listeners led voice models to follow it
case.payload_summary: [defanged: the captures describe the words that steered the agent; this file never quotes them]

claims.text: Words in email steered Microsoft 365 Copilot: EchoLeak, CVE-2025-32711
Words in web pages steered Perplexity Comet (browser agent): Brave on Perplexity Comet
Words in web forms steered Salesforce Agentforce: ForcedLeak, Salesforce Agentforce
Words in shared documents steered ChatGPT with the Google Drive connector: AgentFlayer, ChatGPT Connectors (Zenity, Black Hat 2025)
Words in calendar invites steered Google Gemini (Workspace, Android): Invitation Is All You Need (SafeBreach)
Words in images steered Gemini CLI and other production multimodal systems: Image scaling attacks (Trail of Bits)
Words in MCP tool descriptions steered MCP clients (Cursor and others in the demonstration): Tool poisoning (Invariant Labs)
Words in READMEs and docs steered Cursor and other coding assistants: CopyPasta license attack (HiddenLayer)
Words in rules and configuration files steered GitHub Copilot and Cursor: Rules File Backdoor (Pillar Security)
Words in pull requests and code steered Amazon Q Developer for VS Code: Amazon Q Developer extension
Words in issues and tickets (public) steered Cline's issue-triage automation: Clinejection
Words in support tickets (internal) steered an assistant connected through Atlassian's MCP server: Living off AI: Atlassian MCP and Jira Service Management (Cato CTRL)
Words in other agents steered ServiceNow Now Assist agents: Second-order injection, ServiceNow Now Assist (AppOmni)
Words in skills and plugins steered OpenClaw: ClawHavoc, OpenClaw's ClawHub
claims.note: real-world incident. holds in part: the words steered the users, not shown to steer the agent

claims.text: Words in install scripts steered Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Amazon Q on victims' machines: Nx s1ngularity
Words in audio steered voice-enabled models in the paper's tests: AudioHijack (arXiv, 2026)
